key_insight: A cμ priority rule using effective service rates that account for compute, memory bandwidth, and KV-cache capacity minimizes cumulative holding cost in a fluid model of LLM inference.
engineering_relevance: Memory-aware request prioritization can reduce LLM serving latency while preserving high throughput under constrained GPU memory.
method: Model stochastic, heterogeneous requests as a multiclass queue with prefill, decode, and finite KV-cache capacity.
Derive effective service rates and prove fluid-model optimality of the cμ rule.
Construct a feasible finite-system policy and prove convergence of its scaled dynamics to the optimal fluid policy.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 report substantially lower average latency with high throughput versus existing scheduling policies; the abstract gives no numerical results.
watch_item: Optimality is established in the fluid limit, so finite-system performance and effective-rate estimation require validation for each deployment.
paper_title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
